commit.message:
build: compile the library and the tests without warnings

gcc and clang each had something to say about the library and the test
build; none of it was a real bug, but warnings that are always there are
warnings nobody reads.

  - LensFwd.rf was only filled on the rotational path, and gcc could not
    see that lensFwdApply reads it only there.  Fill it with the identity
    either way -- once per Gauss-Newton iteration, not per point.
  - vsLensUndistortPoint/vsLensDistortPoint returned VS_ERROR without
    writing their outputs.  Callers check the return code, but after
    inlining gcc still saw an indeterminate value at -O3 (bench/build.sh).
    Write the point through unchanged on the failure path.
  - The SSE2-only timing variables in test_contrast.c/test_compareimg.c
    now live under the same #ifdef as their uses; test_motiondetect.c's
    loglevel likewise moves under USE_OMP.  test_transform_baseline.c had
    a genuinely dead packedTol.
  - isnan() in test_lensdistortion.c proved nothing: the tests are built
    with -ffast-math, under which it may fold to 0.  A range check is
    still evaluated, and a NaN fails it.

Also stop the intentional error output from reading like a failing test.
test_vsvector_bounds mutes vs_log_level around the ~1000 calls it expects
to be rejected (with a comment on when to un-mute it); test_frameinfo and
test_serialize_robust keep their handful of Error: lines visible -- muting
there could hide an unexpected one -- but say up front that they are the
expected result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
